name: Australia
lead: There are 11 Michelin star restaurants in Australia, all in South Australia, from the country’s first MICHELIN Guide, announced in Adelaide on 14 October 2026. Magill Estate Restaurant, Penfolds’ dining room in the Adelaide foothills, is the only one with two stars; Sydney and Melbourne have none. Here are their dinner, lunch and wine pairing prices per person, side by side.
intro: Prices are in Australian dollars (A$), with a switch to see them in pounds, euros or US dollars. Prices checked October 2026 and include 10% GST; service isn’t added to the bill.
serviceText: Every figure is for one guest. Australian menu prices include 10% GST and no service charge is added, so these are the full prices before drinks; tipping isn’t expected, though 10% for good service is welcome. Many restaurants add a surcharge of about 10–15% on Sundays and public holidays, and some a small card fee. Prices shown in other currencies use the day’s exchange rate and are approximate.
sourcesText: Dinner is the restaurant’s main tasting or set menu. Many South Australian winery restaurants open mainly at lunch; where a restaurant serves the same menu at lunch and dinner, it’s shown under both. Wine is the wine pairing for that menu where one is offered. Prices come from each restaurant’s own website.
starsText: The Google reviews score out of 5 and the number of reviews, where we have one. Stars come from the first MICHELIN Guide South Australia, announced on 14 October 2026, so there are no earlier star changes to show.
